task_row_model.query: I have a Python recursive Fibonacci with memoization that fails for n > 1000 and suffers recursion overhead. How should I change it to avoid the recursion limit and get O(n) time with O(1) space (if I only need the nth value)?

documents.content: Python's interpreter enforces a recursion depth limit (the default in CPython is around 1000 calls) accessible via sys.getrecursionlimit and adjustable with sys.setrecursionlimit. CPython does not perform tail-call optimization, so deeply recursive functions will still consume stack frames even if written in tail-recursive form. Using functools.lru_cache or a memo dict eliminates repeated computations and yields linear time complexity for many divide-and-conquer recurrences, but memoization does not remove the required recursion depth: the call stack still grows with recursion depth.

Practical comparisons often contrast top-down memoized recursion with bottom-up iteration. Both approaches can achieve O(n) time for simple linear recurrences, but a bottom-up loop avoids function-call overhead and the recursion depth problem. If you need all intermediate results, allocating a list of length n+1 and filling it iteratively is straightforward and uses O(n) extra space. Journalistic benchmarks note that iterative loops in CPython run noticeably faster than equivalent recursive calls due to lower per-call overhead; some commentary adds historical notes about early languages optimizing tail-calls, which CPython does not replicate.

A compact iterative Fibonacci computes the nth value with two variables: initialize a=0, b=1 (handle n==0 return 0; n==1 return 1), then loop n times doing a, b = b, a+b and return a. This simple loop uses O(n) time and only two scalar variables, so O(1) space. Many informal recipes emphasize that if only the final value is required the two-variable method is preferable to storing the whole sequence, and that it both removes recursion and minimizes memory.

Reference entries on dynamic programming often include tree-traversal case studies and definitional boilerplate: memoization caches subproblem results, tabulation fills tables iteratively, and some textbooks digress into unrelated history of algorithmic paradigms. Supplemental sections sometimes present modular arithmetic variants for very large Fibonacci indices and performance statistics from niche implementations, but these tangents are not required for converting a recursive memoized routine into a loop-based implementation.

task_row_model.golden_answer: Replace the recursive memoized routine with a bottom-up iterative loop: handle base cases 0 and 1, set a=0, b=1, then for i in range(n): a, b = b, a+b and return a. Iteration avoids CPython's recursion depth limit (~1000) and per-call overhead, runs in O(n) time, and uses O(1) space when only the nth value is needed. If all values are required, use a preallocated list of size n+1 (O(n) space).
